questions.q: Why does the lesson teach a five-step method instead of a list of known bugs to memorize?
options: Interviewers deliberately write new scenarios, so a repeatable process transfers in a way memorization doesn't
Memorizing bugs is faster and always sufficient for any interview
Solidity only has five possible bugs in total
A method is only useful if you've already seen the exact bug before
questions.explain: The lesson states explicitly that interviewers write unfamiliar scenarios on purpose, which is why a transferable method matters more than memorized examples.

questions.q: In Exercise 1's withdraw function, what specifically causes the reentrancy vulnerability?
options: The external call to msg.sender happens before balances[msg.sender] is decremented
The function uses the keyword external instead of public
The function does not use the unchecked keyword
The function never checks msg.sender's balance at all
questions.explain: The lesson identifies the ordering problem directly: the call happens before the state update, allowing repeated re-entry before the balance reflects the withdrawal.

questions.q: In Exercise 2's unstake function, what effect does wrapping the subtraction in an unchecked block have?
options: It disables Solidity's default underflow protection, letting the value wrap instead of reverting
It automatically doubles the gas cost of the function
It makes the function impossible to call successfully
It has no effect, since unchecked blocks are purely cosmetic
questions.explain: The lesson explains unchecked disables the default revert-on-underflow behavior, letting an excessive amount wrap to a huge number instead.

questions.q: What is the core problem with the setFeeRecipient function in Exercise 3?
options: It changes critical contract state with no access control restricting who can call it
It does not emit an event when the fee recipient changes
It uses the wrong data type for the address parameter
It is marked external instead of internal
questions.explain: The lesson identifies the missing access-control check as the core issue -- any address can redirect fee payments.

questions.q: Why does the lesson recommend narrating your reasoning out loud during a whiteboard review, even before finding the bug?
options: It demonstrates the repeatable process itself, which is often worth more than a fast but silent answer
Interviewers require complete silence until the final answer is given
Narration guarantees the candidate will find every bug in the code
It is only useful for candidates who don't understand the code
questions.explain: The lesson states that walking through the method out loud demonstrates the actual skill being hired for, independent of how quickly the bug is spotted.
